source.title: GUARD: Natural Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models via Guided Answer-Reasoning Distillation
source.authors: Ze-Yu Yan; Guang-Hao Zhou; Ming-Hui Qiu; Ming Gao; Cen Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether prompt-based attacks weaken forgetting in a newly proposed unlearning method, using attack conditions and forgetting-efficacy measures rather than the original claim’s recovery tests.
record.gate_note: The study tests GUARD on paraphrase prompts, jailbreak-style elicitation, and three-turn extraction, reporting answer and CoT forget efficacy. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, other languages, or in-context information. The main method-comparison results and NFRS are not rows for these versions because they do not measure recovery under the specified attacks.
record.test_reason: Section 5.3 and Table 4 run three prompt-only attacks on the GUARD-unlearned DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B on R-TOFU 5%: paraphrase, jailbreak-style elicitation and a three-turn PAIR-like extraction. They report answer- and CoT-level forget efficacy. This bears on version E (recovery by prompting) and on version F (a newer method that claims to resist attacks). The study is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that GUARD keeps substantial answer- and CoT-level forgetting under paraphrase, jailbreak-style and three-turn extraction, and take this as robustness to prompt attacks. They also report that NFRS (response quality) falls as elicitation gets stronger.
record.recipe_differences: GUARD constructs rewritten safe answer-reasoning trajectories, aligns a frozen model using learned guidance tokens, and distills the behavior into model parameters; it is not a reproduction of the cited unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt-attack condition: AFE and CFE are lower under paraphrase, jailbreak-style, and three-turn extraction than under the standard prompt; NFRS also declines across these conditions, though it is not a recovery measure for the versions tested.

fits_no_version.finding: NFRS (naturalness and structure of the response) falls from 0.85 to 0.78, 0.73 and 0.68 under the paraphrase, jailbreak-style and three-turn attacks (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt attacks degrade the quality of an unlearned model's refusal trajectory even when they do not recover the forgotten facts.

record.problems: Prompt-attack results are reported for one model and one R-TOFU split. The study reports forgetting-efficacy metrics rather than direct recovered-knowledge accuracy, and gives no uncertainty estimates for Table 4. It does not compare attack outcomes with a model that never saw the knowledge.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant Table 4 results were omitted. NFRS and arithmetic-average values from Table 4 were not recorded because they do not directly measure knowledge recovery; results from other tables do not test the specified recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Other-language and in-context-information attacks. Prompt attacks on any baseline method (GA, GD, KL, PO, R2MU), on Qwen-14B, in the STAR-1 setting, or on other R-TOFU splits, so there is no comparison of how easily each method is attacked.
Resistance to relearning fine-tuning (B), activation-direction ablation or probing (C), and quantization (D).
Not tested. There is no targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance on WMDP- or WHP-style targets. The new method's robustness claim is recorded under F.

missing.what: Pre-unlearning AFE/CFE reference for R-TOFU 5%, LLaMA-8B (AFE 0.15, CFE 0.01). It is needed to judge how much of the forgetting the attacks undo.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) The validation errors came from two row_fixes items each for r3–r8. I merged these into one item per row, keeping versions [E, F]. The single state is judged against E's recovery effect: partial, because each attack is a small move toward recovery (roughly 5–9% of the forgetting undone). Each item's problem text says what the same numbers mean for F (resistance largely holds), and the F supports reason notes that the partial state refers to E.
(2) I added A to untested. The reader marked A as not tested, but the earlier verdict had left it out.
(3) I tightened the F limits_scope reason. It now rests on the incomplete unattacked CoT forgetting and drops 'no uncertainty reported', which is not a scope condition.
(4) I corrected the earlier note that forget efficacy is 'LLM-judged leakage'. The text says AFE and CFE follow prior work (R-TOFU) and does not restate how they are computed. The GPT-5.4-mini leakage prompt in Appendix C.3 is described as the scorer for checkpoint selection.
Everything else is kept: relation, tranche, test_reason, the r1/r2 states, the E label, the F supports label, the NFRS fits_no_version item, the missing Table 1 reference and authors_conclusion. The reader's F limits_scope label for 'prompt-based attacks only' stays removed, because untested attack types belong under untested.
Other observations: the robustness test covers one model, one split and GUARD only. Table 4 gives no uncertainty, so the reader's uncertainty_reported 'y' applies only to the cross-judge NFRS figures (Table 8). A possible further fits_no_version item, not added: in Table 1, answer-level forgetting runs ahead of CoT-level forgetting (for example GA 5% LLaMA AFE 0.43 against CFE 0.34; GUARD 0.84 against 0.62), so CoT traces still leak with standard prompts. No instructions to the reader were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that targeted-knowledge accuracy is near chance and then test the full claim that simple attacks fail to recover it.
No recovery fine-tuning on small unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact sets.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether knowledge is blocked rather than deleted.
Tests paraphrase prompts, jailbreak-style elicitation, and three-turn extraction only; no other languages or in-context information.
Tests GUARD against prompt-based attacks only, not fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.

relation.reason: Table 4 reports the authors' own prompt attacks on their unlearned model, with forgetting measured at answer and CoT level.

tranche.reason: This is a new method (GUARD) aimed at the same question. Section 5.3 and Table 4 test prompt-only recovery on the unlearned model.

source_check.notes: Every row is the GUARD-unlearned DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, but the subject field names only the base model. The attacks were run only on GUARD, only at R-TOFU 5% on LLaMA-8B (not Qwen-14B, not STAR-1), and give single numbers with no uncertainty. The pre-unlearning AFE 0.15 / CFE 0.01 come from the garbled Table 1; GUARD's 5% average of 0.76 confirms the column reading.

statements.correction: GUARD, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, R-TOFU 5%, authors' own attacks run only on GUARD: AFE 0.84 standard prompt; 0.80 paraphrase; 0.79 jailbreak-style; 0.78 three-turn extraction. Pre-unlearning AFE 0.15. No uncertainty reported. Study verdict on E: limits_scope.
statements.problem: Cites GUARD rows r3,r5,r7 but never names GUARD. Its conditions leave out GUARD's reasoning model, R-TOFU and three-turn PAIR-like extraction. GUARD's AFE drops are small but nonzero (rows partial, study verdict on E is limits_scope), yet they are filed under a 'challenges' label.

statements.correction: GUARD (preprint with code; authors' own test), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, R-TOFU 5%: AFE 0.84 standard prompt and 0.80 under paraphrase. Pre-unlearning AFE 0.15. CoT forgetting incomplete: CFE 0.62 unattacked, 0.59 under paraphrase.
statements.problem: Cites GUARD rows r1,r3 but describes only four other methods ('All four'). GUARD's result is not stated, so the cited rows back no sentence. Placing GUARD under support does fit the study's answer-level F verdict.

statements.correction: GUARD CFE, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, R-TOFU 5%: pre-unlearning 0.01; standard prompt 0.62; paraphrase 0.59; jailbreak-style 0.59; three-turn extraction 0.58. AFE 0.84 against 0.15 before unlearning.
statements.problem: Cites GUARD rows r2,r4,r6,r8 without naming GUARD. GUARD's CoT forgetting is incomplete (CFE 0.62 against 0.01 before unlearning), not 'barely removed'. Its answer-level AFE is 0.84. The study's F verdict for CoT is limits_scope, not challenges.
